{{Quote|THE GALAXY'S BEST-SELLING NEWSPAPER|Headline for ''The Coruscant Holo Net''|<ref name="Who was Zatch" />}}
'''''The Coruscant Holo Net''''' was a newspaper in print that was published on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], during the two last [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] of that government. Although officially aligned with the Republic, that paper sometimes contained advertisments that went against the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]] or had ties with the enemy [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist Alliance]]. [[Keets Freely]], its [[Chief Reporter]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], was among the first individuals to ever suspect the then-[[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] carried a hidden agenda. In the wake of the war and after the [[Declaration of a New Order|birth]] of Palpatine's [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the publication of ''The Coruscant Holo Net'' was discontinued and Freely was branded a traitor by the new regime.

==History==
[[File:Chancellor_safe.png|thumb|left|250px|Tho-Masfran Ciss' report on a failed assassination attempt on Palpatine]]
{{Quote|He was a journalist, writing for the Coruscant Holo Net. One of the first to ask why Palpatine was grabbing all the power even while he was smiling at us, telling us he was protecting us.|[[Dexter Jettster/Legends|Dexter Jettster]], on Keets Freely|<ref name="TLotJ3" />}}
Established in [[48 BBY/Legends|48 BBY]], ''The Coruscant Holo Net'' was still widely distributed during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], for the price of 1 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]]. At that [[Time/Legends|time]], its [[Journalist/Legends|journalism]] staff included [[Senior Reporter]] [[Nik Kigee]],<ref name="Who was Zatch" /> [[Senior Coruscant Correspondent]] [[Tho-Masfran Ciss]],<ref name="Chancellor Safe" /> and [[Chief Reporter]] [[Keets Freely]].<ref name="War on Wookiee World" />
Shortly before the outbreak of the conflict, Ciss chronicled the failed [[Plot to assassinate Chancellor Palpatine|assassination plot]] carried out by a group of [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] on the person of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and the subsquent ascension of [[Security Advisor]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] to the position of [[Junior Representative/Legends|Junior Representative]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="Chancellor Safe" /> At some point, Freely discovered a scandal involving the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] and the Supreme Chancellor. It appeared that the Chancellor had helped the Banking Clan develop a complex system of secret, tax-free bank accounts for megacorporations on a ring of planets. This allowed Palpatine to garner the support of both the Banking Clan and the largest corporations in the galaxy. When his editor refused to publish that discovery, Freely resigned from the agency.<ref name="TLotJ9">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Master of Deception]]''</ref> The paper's existence was discontinued shortly after the [[Declaration of a New Order|foundation]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], and its former Chief Reporter was given a death mark, becoming a target of the [[Enemy Eradication Order of Coruscant]].<ref name="TLotJ3">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref>

==Content==
[[File:Dubious_ad.png|thumb|right|250px|An example of a dubious advertisement published in the paper]]
{{Quote|INCOMPETENT: Where were the Coruscant Guards when Seppie killers invaded the capital?|Tho-Masfran Ciss|<ref name="Chancellor Safe" />}}
Every issue ''The Coruscant Holo Net'' typically contained new articles and multiple advertisements, [[Writing/Legends|written]] entirely in the [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]]. Despite its proclaimed Republican affiliation,<ref name="Chancellor Safe" /> ''The Coruscant Holo Net'' sometimes included content that went against the Republic's laws. One issue contained a cryptic advertisement invited the readers to contact the [[Separatist Senate/Legends|parliament]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist Alliance]] on [[Raxus Secundus/Legends|Raxus Secundus]] and ask "[[Grievous/Legends|the General]]" in order to purchase [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]].<ref name="Who was Zatch" /> On another occasion, the paper published a classified ad that promoted [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]],<ref name="War on Wookiee World" /> while the ''[[Rights of Sentience]]'' clause of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]] strictly forbade it.<ref name="COD">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref>

==Known issues==
*[[The Coruscant Holo Net: Chancellor Safe|''Chancellor Safe'']], published in [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], covered the [[Plot to assassinate Chancellor Palpatine|plot to assassinate]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="Chancellor Safe" />
*[[The Coruscant Holo Net: War on Wookiee World?|''War on Wookiee World?'']], published in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], covered the [[Battle on an unidentified farming moon|battle]] on a [[Unidentified farming moon|farming moon]] in orbit of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].<ref name="War on Wookiee World" />
*[[The Coruscant Holo Net: Who was "Zatch"?|''Who was "Zatch"?'']], published in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], covered the [[Ambush of the Goldskin Parade|ambush]] of the [[Goldskin Parade]].<ref name="Who was Zatch" />
*[[The Coruscant Holo Net: Ru-ful War|''Ru-ful War'']], published in 20 BBY, covered the [[Battle of Phorose|battle]] of [[Phorose]].<ref name="Ru-ful War" />
